column2: Property Validation Issues with new Form Engine
column16:
First thing I noticed is in the case where a property does not get cast into the expected type correctly, resulting in the value being sent to the back end being an empty string.
In the screenshot below you will see the 'limit' key have a value of """" even though the value typed in is not an empty string. This then causes the back end to report a missing required property, rather than the type being wrong for the value given for the property expected NUMBER got STRING would be the correct message given if UI passed the correct value.

second I have noticed some weird behavior in the Catalog Delete snap where validation errors are being reported in the response given to UI yet nothing is presented to the user. I also have noticed when one of the fields changes in value with expression enabled off, the save icon stays un-clickable and gets erased when I validate the snap. Screenshots are shown below.

The first screenshot shows the response from backend reporting missing property, the second screenshot is showing the value being changed from empty to 'm' and the save icon still does not become clickable. Third screenshot shows the value as empty with no error given after validation, the fourth screenshot shows the first issue mentioned above where the casted type error results in the empty string being passed to the back end resulting in the 'missing property’ error, which is a bit confusing and not helpful to the user since they have a value typed in, just not the right type.

4. Tasks should be migrated and the pipeline reference should be resolved if the pipeline is migrated as well,

column10:
Create a prject with the following assets:
- 1 master pipeline which has references to accounts (Mysql snap), tasks (Task execute), File (File reader), pipeline (For each, nested,pipeline execute snap) 
- 1 pipeline containing a simple snap (to be used as child for scheduled tasks, triggered tasks, nested, pipeline execute snap and for each snap)
- 1 Ultra task compatible pipeline for the ultra tasks
- 1 Ultra task that is in disabled state
- 1 Ultra task that is in enabled state
- 1 Scheduled task
- 1 triggered task (to be used in the master pipeline with task execute snap)

column2: Ultra pipeline runtime stats are reported once the CP is up and running
column10:
Steps to follow:-
1. Create an ultra task and feed some messages to ultra pipeline. Goto dashboard and verify the processed doc count. 
2. Break outbound http and https connection to control plane using following iptables commands, 
sudo iptables -A OUTPUT -d (ex:canary.elastic.snaplogicdev.com) -p tcp --dport 80 -m state --state NEW,ESTABLISHED -j DROP sudo iptables -A OUTPUT -d (ex:canary.elastic.snaplogicdev.com) -p tcp --dport 443 -m state --state NEW,ESTABLISHED -j DROP

3. Break input connection from control plane to plex using,

sudo iptables -I INPUT -s (ex:canary.elastic.snaplogicdev.com) -j DROP (drop all in bound connection)

4. Go to dashboard and check health page, in few seconds you can see the plex nodes count becomes zero.
5. Feed more messages(I used curl to feed doc) and verify the response of curl command(should be 200 OK with expected output of pipeline and headers in response) 
6. Goto dashboard and in pipeline tab you can still see the ultra pipeline up and running(started state) but the doc count is not incrementing as the communication with control plane is broken.
7. Feed some more doc and verify.
This is working in the same way as explained above for 1 hr. After 1 hr feed message is failing(PLAT-7257).
8. Now reestablish the connection by running,
 sudo iptables -F
9. After few seconds, you can see all the messages are properly displayed in extra details tab in ultra task’s execution status popup.
 
Step no 4 and 6 are the indicators for broken connection with control plane. 
Also we can access local dashboard to see the status while control plane communication is broken(https://:8084 and https://:8090)

1. Create a simple pipeline, create an ultra task and feed some messages to ultra pipeline. Goto dashboard and verify the processed doc count.

	- Break outbound http and https connection to control plane using following iptables commands, (DO NOT ADD cdn. IN THE POD URL)
		- sudo iptables -A OUTPUT -d <pod_name>(ex:canary.elastic.snaplogic.com) -p tcp --dport 80 -m state --state NEW,ESTABLISHED -j DROP
		- sudo iptables -A OUTPUT -d <pod-name>(ex:canary.elastic.snaplogic.com) -p tcp --dport 443 -m state --state NEW,ESTABLISHED -j DROP
	- Break input connection from control plane to plex using,(DO NOT ADD cdn. IN THE POD URL)
		- sudo iptables -I INPUT -s <pod-name or ip>(ex:canary.elastic.snaplogic.com) -j DROP (drop all in bound connection)
	- Repeat step 2 for regular nodes as well	
3. Go to dashboard -> Health tab, in few seconds the plex nodes count becomes zero.
4. Feed more messages(using curl / postman) and verify the response of request should be 200 OK with expected output of pipeline and headers in response

6. Feed some more docs and verify. Check after 1-2 hours and verify step 5 (PLAT-7257).
7. Now re-establish the connection by running below command,
 		- sudo iptables -F
 		- Repeat step 7 for regular nodes as well
